newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan upbeat over weekend talks with Peru rebels.
newsitem.headline: Japan upbeat over weekend talks with Peru rebels.

text.p: Gloom has turned to optimism in Japan after news that talks were due to resume between Peru and guerrillas holding 74 hostages in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, a Foreign Ministry official said on Saturday.

The Foreign Ministry was upbeat in the wake of Friday's statement by Peruvian Prime Minister Alberto Pandolfi that negotiations between Education Minister Domingo Palermo and the leftist Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) were expected to resume.

"The mood has changed. Until now it has been a stalemate, but after yesterday's press conference by Pandolfi in which he said talks would restart over the weekend, it seems there is some movement," the ministry official said.

Japan has said earlier the crisis had become more serious than ever as hostage releases had trimmed the number of people still detained -- including Japanese Ambassador Morihisa Aoki, Peruvian Foreign Minister Francisco Tudela and top echelon anti-terrorist, army and air force officers -- down to a manageable number for the guerrillas.

Pandolfi told reporters on Friday that Palermo, President Fujimori's appointed negotiator, had spoken face-to-face with Nestor Cerpa, the leader of the MRTA rebels in the besieged residence, on December 28.
Pandolfi told reporters on Thursday that Peru might let the rebels leave the country if the hostage crisis ended peacefully.
